description: Pin assignment for the agentic keyboard expansion baseboard. The dev board plugs into the baseboard via a 44P header. Verified against Tuya official pinmux + tuya_t5ai_core.c board driver. Board revision v1.2 (WS2812 P13->P4/SPI1_MOSI, LCD_BL P5->P8, FPC1 pad order fixed; net-verified 2026-09-01).

board_occupied.use: SPI1_SCK (reserved for WS2812 SPI1 group, no external load)
SPI1_CS (reserved for WS2812 SPI1 group, no external load)
SPI1_MISO (reserved for WS2812 SPI1 group; freed from LCD_BL in v1.2)

assigned.note: v1.2: 3x WS2812 daisy-chain driven by the official SPI WS2812 driver over SPI1 (MOSI=P4), level-shifted 3.3V->5V via SN74LV1T34. TKL initialises the whole SPI1 group P2/P3/P4/P5; only MOSI carries data. P13 (v1.0 GPIO bit-bang pin, failed timing) released to NC.

lcd_spi.note: Reuses the board's official ST7789 wiring; firmware only changes resolution to 320x240.

header_44p.note: 44P = two 1x22 headers J1 + J2, from T5AI-Core_V101-SCH.pdf. Only pins listed here are broken out; P28/P33/P35 are NOT on the header (do not use).
header_44p.row_spacing_note: Center-to-center distance between J1 and J2 rows, caliper-measured 2026-08-21. Use this for the two 1x22 socket footprints on the baseboard.

expansion_usb.note: Expansion-board Type-C for firmware flash + comms. T5 has NO USB device; a CH340C USB-to-UART bridge provides the CDC. Shares UART0 (P10/P11) with the dev board's onboard CH342F (plug only ONE Type-C at a time). Auto-reset/download via CH340C DTR/RTS -> S8050 -> T5_RST, mirroring the dev board's circuit. USB isolation: the Type-C D+/D- connect ONLY to the CH340C; they are NOT wired to the header DP/DN pins (which are the dev board T5's USB Host signals, a separate USB). The expansion board does not use/route header DP/DN.
expansion_usb.tx_isolation: series 2k resistor (stock C60488) on CH340C TX -> T5 RX to reduce bus contention with onboard CH342F. 2k chosen (stock, RC effect negligible at 460800 baud).
expansion_usb.auto_reset: Mirrors dev board SCH (U2 CH342F, single S8050 transistor Q2): RTS0 -> Q2 base (direct); DTR0 -> R22(4.7k) -> Q2 base; Q2 collector -> R14(100R) -> T5_RST (J2.2); Q2 emitter -> GND. T5_RST pull-up R47(10k) + C51(0.1uF) already on dev board.
expansion_usb.vbus: Type-C VBUS(5V) powers ONLY the CH340C locally via a small 3.3V LDO (HE9073A33M5R, SOT-23-5, stock). DOES NOT feed the system (NOT connected to header 5V). This lets flashing/comms work even with a dead battery / unpowered system.
expansion_usb.ch340c_supply: Type-C VBUS 5V -> LDO 3.3V -> CH340C VCC. CH340C IO = 3.3V, directly matches T5 UART (no over-voltage). Independent of battery.

battery.note: Expansion battery connector in PARALLEL with the dev board's JST on the SAME BAT net. Only ONE cell plugged at a time. NO charge management on the expansion board (uses dev board ETA6003).
battery.power_switch: Battery main switch (SK12D07VG5, C431548, slide/toggle, stock) in series on BAT+ of the expansion cell. Gates ONLY the battery path. Type-C stays powered/charging regardless.

ws2812.note: 3x WS2812 RGB LED daisy-chain, single data line, 5V powered. T5 3.3V GPIO -> SN74LV1T34 level shifter -> 5V DIN.
ws2812.note_v12: v1.2: moved from P13 (GPIO bit-bang, failed nanosecond timing on dual-core + PM) to P4=SPI1_MOSI with the official SPI WS2812 driver (waveform from SPI peripheral). SPI1 group P2/P3/P4/P5 reserved.

resolved: 44P header per-pin positions: from T5AI-Core_V101-SCH.pdf (J1/J2, 1x22 each)
